title: Trade Liberalization, Export and Product Innovation
abstract: arXiv:2603.23825v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: This paper studies firms' optimal response to a trade liberalization shock in terms of export and product innovation both theoretically and empirically. We find that trade liberalization, namely China's WTO accession, reduces iceberg trade cost by around 13%, thus promoting export participation. Subsequently, it affects firms' product innovation through both contemporaneous and dynamic channels. First, it incentivizes firms to innovate as the marginal benefit of innovation for exporting firms is higher than that for non-exporting firms. Second, as a firm starts to innovate, it predicts to have a higher probability of moving to a better productivity state and can save the entry cost of innovation in the future, resulting in additional dynamic benefits which are quantitatively substantial in our estimations. Such an innovation-promotion effect is an unintended consequence of trade liberalization.

translated_title: 贸易自由化、出口与产品创新
translated_abstract: 本文从理论和实证两方面研究了企业对贸易自由化冲击的最优反应，涉及出口和产品创新。我们发现，贸易自由化，即中国加入世界贸易组织（WTO），将冰山贸易成本降低了约13%，从而促进了出口参与。随后，它通过同期和动态渠道影响企业的产品创新。首先，它激励企业进行创新，因为出口企业的创新边际收益高于非出口企业。其次，当企业开始创新时，它预测自己进入更好生产率状态的概率更高，并能节省未来的创新进入成本，从而产生额外的动态收益，在我们的估计中这些收益在数量上相当可观。这种创新促进效应是贸易自由化的一个意外后果。
tldr: 本文发现中国加入WTO带来的贸易自由化不仅通过降低贸易成本促进出口，还通过同期和动态渠道显著激励企业产品创新，且这种创新促进效应是贸易自由化的意外后果。
en_tdlr: This paper finds that trade liberalization via China's WTO accession not only promotes exports by reducing trade costs but also significantly incentivizes product innovation through contemporaneous and dynamic channels, with this innovation-promotion effect being an unintended consequence.
